questions.question: Describe the most densely populated regions of the world.
questions.expected_answer: Asia has by far the most people, about six in ten of the world's people. India and China each have more than one point four billion people. South Asia, including India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, East Asia, including eastern China and Japan, and Java in Southeast Asia are very crowded. Other crowded regions are Europe, the north-east United States, West Africa, especially Nigeria, the Nile valley and the Great Lakes of East Africa.

questions.question: Describe four types of sparsely populated regions and explain why few people live there.
questions.expected_answer: Hot deserts such as the Sahara have very little water. Cold areas such as Siberia, northern Canada and Antarctica have long, freezing winters, and Antarctica has no permanent population. Tropical rainforests such as the Amazon have dense forest, poor soil and disease, which make travel and farming difficult. High mountains such as the Himalayas are cold, steep, hard to farm and have thin air.

questions.question: Explain the positive and negative factors that affect world population distribution.
questions.expected_answer: Positive factors attract people: flat, fertile river plains and deltas such as the Ganges, Yangtze and Nile, a moderate climate with reliable rain such as monsoon rains for rice, coasts for trade and fishing, and resources, industry, jobs and services. Negative factors discourage settlement: climates that are too cold or too dry, steep or high land, dense forest, poor soil and disease. History also matters, as river valleys farmed for thousands of years built up large populations.
